Jordan (ACME): Hey, seeing intermittent 502s in the UI when I press Run. Error shows "Something went wrong". Request ID in response header: req_9a2f4c. Happens ~1/10 runs. Chrome 117 macOS. Can you tell me what to capture?

Lina (Support): Sorry about that, Jordan. Yes — please capture a network export (HAR) + console logs and upload. Also include the failing request id and a curl repro if you can. Quick steps for Chrome below.

Sam (Eng): Tip: we look for the response headers (x-request-id / x-rw-req-id) and the full request/response bodies. If you can reproduce, run a curl with `-v` or `-D -` so we get headers.

Lina (Support): Chrome (desktop) capture steps:
1) Open DevTools: Cmd+Option+I (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+I (Win).
2) Network tab -> check "Preserve log".
3) DevTools settings (gear) -> Network -> check "Disable cache" while DevTools is open.
4) Reproduce the error in the UI.
5) Right-click the list of network entries -> "Save all as HAR with content" (this includes request/response bodies).
6) Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." or select messages -> copy -> paste into console.txt (include stack traces).
7) Zip the HAR + console.txt and name it like `acme_req_9a2f4c_har.zip`.

Lina (Support): Example curl to capture headers & body (replace <TOKEN> and <URL>):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "x-rw-req-id: req_9a2f4c" -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
Run that from terminal; the `-v` will print response headers we need. If the request is proxied through the UI, try to copy the exact request payload from the HAR and use it in curl.

Jordan (ACME): How do I include stack traces from the console?

Sam (Eng): In Console -> click the message to expand, then right-click the expanded frame -> "Copy stack" or use "Save as...". If you see "(anonymous)" frames, expand the source link to get the full trace.

Lina (Support): If you're on Firefox: DevTools -> Network -> right-click -> "Save all as HAR". Safari: Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> Right-click -> "Export HAR" (older Safari versions may require the network export extension). Full debug-bundle docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/debug-bundles

Lina (Support): When you upload, please include: repro steps (short), URL, user id (or test account), time window, browser+version, and the file. If the UI shows a request id (like `req_9a2f4c`) put it in the filename and in the message body.

debug-bot: Created ticket #2345 for Jordan — label: support/needs-repro.

Jordan (ACME): Uploading now: acme_req_9a2f4c_har.zip (just posted to this thread).

Lina (Support): Got it, thanks! We'll pull the HAR and the server logs matching `req_9a2f4c` and update you. Expect first triage within 1 business day. :thumbsup:

Sam (Eng): If we can't reproduce locally we'll ask for a short screen recording + the HAR. Also may ask for the exact time of the failed run so we can tail the gateway logs for the req id.

Jordan (ACME): Noted — thanks everyone, uploading helped.
